jobs.title: Vice President of Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President of Finance

 

About the Role

 

Quindar is looking for a Vice President of Finance to build and lead the financial team as the company enters its next stage of growth. This person will own financial planning, reporting, budgeting, audit readiness, and capital planning while giving the leadership team a clear view of company performance and the financial implications of key decisions.

 

This is a hands-on leadership role. The VP of Finance should be equally comfortable building a financial model, reviewing departmental spend with a functional leader, preparing materials for the Board, managing an external audit, and supporting financing discussions.

 

What You’ll Do

 

Financial Planning & Analysis

 

 - Own Quindar’s company wide financial model, annual operating plan, forecasts, and long-range financial planning.

 - Maintain accurate forecasts for revenue, expenses, cash, headcount, bookings, ARR, backlog, and other key operating metrics.

 - Build scenario models that help leadership evaluate hiring, investments, facilities, contracts, and strategic initiatives.

 - Provide clear visibility into cash runway, burn, capital requirements, and the financial impact of major company decisions.

 - Review pricing models and active margin profiles.

 - Continuously improve forecasting accuracy as the company scales.

 

Company Metrics, Board & Investor Reporting

 

 - Own the financial and operating metrics used by the executive team, investors, and Board.

 - Maintain a consistent source of truth for KPIs across bookings, ARR, revenue, gross margin, burn, headcount, pipeline, retention, and other company metrics.

 - Prepare financial analysis and supporting materials for Board meetings, investor updates, fundraising, and strategic planning.

 - Translate financial performance into clear insights: what changed, why it changed, and what leadership should do about it.

 

Budgeting & Business Partnership

 

 - Own departmental budgets and work directly with functional leaders to establish financial plans aligned with company priorities.

 - Provide leaders with regular budget vs. actuals reporting, forecasts, and recommendations.

 - Hold teams accountable to financial commitments while helping them understand the tradeoffs behind resource allocation.

 - Build processes that allow managers to make faster, better informed spending and hiring decisions.

 

Accounting, Audit & Financial Controls

 

 - Oversee the relationship with outsourced accounting, tax, and other financial service providers.

 - Lead Quindar’s annual financial statement audit and manage the external audit firm from planning through completion.

 - Ensure the company maintains audit ready financial records, appropriate controls, reconciliations, documentation, and accounting policies.

 - Own the financial close process and continuously improve the timeliness and accuracy of monthly and quarterly reporting.

 - Partner with Legal, Contracts, and Operations on revenue recognition, government contracts, cost allocation, compliance, and other financial requirements.

 

Government Contract Finance

 

 - Serve as the finance owner for Quindar’s government contracts, covering milestone-based billing and collections, cost allocation across programs, and the financial requirements that come with federal contracting.

 - Build and maintain the systems and controls needed for government contract compliance (e.g., DCAA/FAR-oriented requirements, cost accounting, and any incurred-cost or program reporting obligations), and partner with Legal, Contracts, and Operations on new and existing awards.

 

Capital Strategy & Financing

 

 - Support future equity fundraising, including financial diligence, investor materials, data rooms, modeling, and management presentations.

 - Support debt-backed financing and other capital strategies, including lender diligence, covenant modeling, liquidity planning, and ongoing reporting requirements.

 - Maintain relationships with banks, lenders, auditors, insurance providers, and other financial partners.

 - Help leadership evaluate the appropriate mix of equity, debt, and internally generated cash as Quindar scales.

 

Scaling the Finance Function

 

 - Build the processes, systems, reporting infrastructure, and financial controls required for a rapidly growing company.

 - Hire and develop a high-performing finance team as company complexity increases.

 - Prepare Quindar for the financial rigor expected of a later-stage venture-backed company, government contractor, and ultimately a much larger enterprise.

 

What We’re Looking For

 

 - 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including meaningful leadership responsibility in a high growth company.

 - Experience owning FP&A, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and company wide financial models.

 - Demonstrated experience leading annual financial audits and working directly with external audit firms.

 - Experience supporting institutional fundraising, Board reporting, and investor diligence.

 - Experience with debt financing, credit facilities, venture debt, or other lender backed financing.

 - Strong understanding of GAAP accounting and the relationship between accounting, FP&A, and operational decision making.

 - Ability to build financial infrastructure without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

 - Strong analytical judgment and the ability to turn complex financial information into clear recommendations.

 - Comfortable operating at both the strategic and detailed levels from Board conversations to reviewing individual budget variances.

 - Experience in defense contracting or another complex B2B environment is strongly preferred.

 

ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 

Why you'll love working at Quindar

 

 - We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

 - We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

 - Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

 - Each year we have an annual company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Palm Springs, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
Chief of Staff

 

About the Role

 

Quindar is looking for a Chief of Staff to increase the effectiveness and leverage of the CEO as the company scales. This role is 12 – 24 months where you will then have the opportunity to become a key lead in the company. Future founders are also encouraged to apply.

 

The Chief of Staff will help drive the CEO’s highest-priority initiatives, prepare for critical internal and external engagements, run the CEO-facing leadership cadence, and take ownership of high-priority special projects.

 

The Chief of Staff coordinates across executives and functions to turn CEO priorities into action and ensure important work does not stall.

 

What You’ll Do

 

Drive CEO Priorities

 - Translate CEO priorities into clear actions, owners, deadlines, and decisions.

 - Keep critical initiatives moving when the CEO is focused on customers, fundraising, or other priorities.

 - Surface blockers and determine where CEO involvement is actually required.

 - Serve as a thought partner to the CEO on strategic and organizational issues.

 

Executive Communications & Preparation

 - Prepare presentations, briefing materials, talking points, and decision memos for Board, investor, commercial/governments customers, and partner engagements.

 - Support company-wide and executive communications.

 - Turn complex topics into concise narratives, recommendations, and decisions.

 - Coordinate inputs and preparation for high-stakes meetings – typically related to U.S. National Security.

 

Leadership Cadence & Follow-Through

 - Prepare agendas for leadership meetings around priorities, week-over-week changes, risks, and decisions required.

 - Pre-wire important topics with the appropriate executives.

 - Track decisions, actions, owners, and deadlines and ensure follow-through.

 - Partner with Business Operations on company metrics, planning, and underlying operating processes.

 

Own Special Projects

 - Take ownership of urgent or strategic initiatives that do not have a natural owner or require CEO-level attention.

 - Create structure around ambiguous problems and drive them through resolution.

 - Coordinate cross-functional initiatives spanning Growth, Product, Engineering, Programs, and Operations.

 - Support initiatives such as major captures, partnerships, executive hiring, AI adoption, fundraising, or critical customer situations.

 

What We’re Looking For

 - Understanding of National Security programs and initiatives

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.

 - Strong operator who can take an ambiguous problem from idea through execution.

 - High ownership, urgency, and a bias toward closing loops.

 - Excellent judgment and ability to work independently with senior executives.

 - Strong analytical skills and comfort with business, financial, and operating metrics.

 - Ability to move fluidly between strategy and detailed execution.

 - Low ego and comfortable influencing without formal authority.

 

ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 

Why you'll love working at Quindar

 

 - We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

 - We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

 - Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

 - Annually we have a 4-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!

jobs.title: People Operations Manager
jobs.description:
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

The People Operations Manager will oversee the employee lifecycle at Quindar—from recruiting and onboarding through ongoing employee support and offboarding. This is a broad, hands-on role that combines human resources, hiring, event planning, workplace programs, and employment compliance.

You will serve as a trusted resource for employees and managers while ensuring that our people practices are organized, consistent, compliant, and aligned with Quindar’s culture. The right person enjoys creating structure, solving practical problems, and shifting comfortably between strategic projects and day-to-day execution.

This role reports to Business Operations Manager.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

People Operations and Employee Experience

 - Manage core people operations across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee changes, leave, benefits administration, and offboarding.

 - Serve as a responsive and trusted point of contact for employee questions.

 - Maintain accurate employee records, policies, templates, and internal documentation.

 - Coordinate benefits enrollment, renewals, and employee communications in partnership with brokers and vendors.

 - Support performance-review, compensation-review, employee-engagement, and professional-development processes.

 - Help managers navigate employee relations and people-management questions with consistency and good judgment.

 - Build scalable processes that preserve a thoughtful, high-quality employee experience as Quindar grows.

 - Manage relationships with relevant HR, benefits, payroll, recruiting, and employment vendors.

Compliance and Risk Management

 - Maintain compliance with applicable federal, state, and local employment requirements.

 - Coordinate required filings, notices, workplace postings, training, and recordkeeping.

 - Keep employee handbooks and people policies current in partnership with legal counsel and external advisors.

 - Support compliance related to hiring, worker classification, compensation, leave, benefits, accommodations, and terminations.

 - Track changes in employment requirements and recommend updates to Quindar’s policies and practices.

 - Support employment-related audits, diligence requests, and government or customer reporting requirements.

Recruiting and Hiring

 - Partner with hiring managers to define roles, create job descriptions, and develop hiring plans.

 - Manage job postings, applicant tracking, interview scheduling, and candidate communications.

 - Source and screen candidates for selected roles.

 - Design organized and equitable interview processes, including scorecards and interviewer guidance.

 - Coordinate offers, reference checks, background checks, and pre-employment requirements.

 - Monitor recruiting activity and help improve time-to-hire, candidate experience, and hiring quality.

 - Develop talent pipelines and strengthen Quindar’s employer brand.

Events and Culture

 - Plan and execute company offsites, team gatherings, celebrations, and other employee events.

 - Manage event logistics, including schedules, venues, travel, lodging, catering, vendors, budgets, and communications.

 - Develop programs and rituals that strengthen connection and collaboration across the company.

 - Gather employee feedback and continually improve company events and the broader employee experience.

 - Support internal communications and company-wide meetings as needed.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of experience in people operations, human resources, recruiting, or a related role.

 - Experience independently managing multiple stages of the employee lifecycle.

 - Experience in a startup, technology company, aerospace company, or other highly regulated environment.

 - Working knowledge of U.S. employment practices and compliance requirements.

 - Experience coordinating recruiting processes and delivering a strong candidate experience.

 - Demonstrated ability to plan complex events, manage vendors, and stay within budget.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - Excellent organization, follow-through, and attention to detail.

 - Sound judgment and the ability to handle sensitive situations with empathy and discretion.

 - A practical, service-oriented approach paired with a willingness to improve inefficient processes.

 - Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities may evolve.

 - Proficiency with HRIS, applicant-tracking, payroll, benefits, and collaboration tools.
   
   Nice to Have
   
   - Experience supporting a distributed, hybrid, or multi-state workforce.
   
   - Experience working with a professional employer organization or employer-of-record provider.
   
   - Familiarity with immigration coordination, government contracting requirements, or security-related workforce processes.
   
   - Experience implementing or migrating HR systems.
   
   - Relevant certification, such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR.


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 - To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicants must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (also known as a green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.


WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT QUINDAR

 - We work in a cutting-edge industry, and you will have the opportunity to be part of a small team with a direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions.

 - We take work-life balance seriously. We require employees to take at least 15 days off, provide unlimited PTO, and observe most U.S. federal holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical health, so we provide quarterly health and wellness benefits.

 - We provide comprehensive health insurance for employees and their families, with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide a 4% 401(k) match.

 - Each year, we hold a four-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Palm Springs, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company are evolving. You will play an important role in creating the next major—or minor—version!
